title: OTLP remote_write compression + schema-evolution for tenant-aware metrics gateway
creator: Priya Raman
description: Build an OTLP-to-Prometheus remote_write compressor and schema-evolution layer for the metric gateway so we can: (1) reduce egress cost from edge and dedicated nodes by delta/dictionary compression, (2) safely evolve metric/label schemas across tenants, and (3) provide robust dead-letter/backpressure handling for tenant spikes. This ticket covers design, PoC, integration tests, and a canary rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline compresses OTLP metric bundles with >=3x average compression ratio for repeated label patterns on benchmark workload
remote_write output is compatible with Prometheus remote_write ingestion and our existing downsample/rollup pipeline with no loss of metric identity (label canonicalization spec enforced)
Schema evolution mechanism supports two schema versions simultaneously during rollout and silently migrates upgrade-compatible labels without data loss
Backpressure exposed via metrics (gateway_queue_fill, tenant_backpressure_count) and circuit opens when tenant queue > 95% for >30s
Dead-letter queue persists malformed or exceeding-size payloads for later replay with tenant and request metadata
Integration tests covering tenant isolation (no cross-tenant label bleed) and end-to-end roundtrip correctness
Canary rollout executed to 3 customers with monitoring dashboards and a rollback plan
implementation_plan: Design: define compression codec (dictionary + delta + gzip fallback) and label canonicalization rules — doc: https://confluence.redwood/example-metric-compression
PoC: implement compression/decompression shim in gateway sidecar, include checksum and schema_version header
Schema evolution: implement schema registry for metric contract with compatibility checks and promotion API
Backpressure/queueing: add per-tenant leaky-bucket queues with persistent tombstone storage for DLQ
Testing: synthetic benchmark generator (tenant-varied label cardinality) and unit/integration test suite
Observability: add compression_ratio, tenant_queue_fill, remote_write_latency, dlq_events metrics and Grafana dashboard
Rollout: internal canary -> partner customers -> general availability with migration runbook
progress_updates: 2025-01-20: Initial design review completed with Platform and Runtime teams. Agreed on dictionary-first compression with gzip fallback for rare cases.
2025-01-28: PoC compression shim committed (github.com/redwood/telemetry-gateway/pull/402). Basic decompress unit tests added.
2025-02-05: Schema registry prototype sketched. Decided on semantic versioning for schema and 'label_alias' map to handle renamed labels.
2025-02-11: Discovered edge case where tenant label collisions occur when labels arrive in different order. Implementing canonical sort + stable hashing as mitigation.
2025-02-18: Benchmarks against dedicated-node replay workload show 3.6x median compression and 2.1x worst-case. Recording dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/d/metrics/comp-ratio
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Compression adds CPU overhead on edge nodes -> Mitigation: CPU cost measured in PoC, introduce cpu_threshold config and gzip-fallback for low-CPU mode
Risk: Schema mismatch causing silent metric loss -> Mitigation: conservative compatibility rules and schema registry with strict validation during ingest
Risk: DLQ growth leading to storage pressure -> Mitigation: DLQ retention policy, tenant quotas, and automated paging to S3
Risk: Increased latency for small bursts -> Mitigation: adaptive batching based on latency SLO vs compression benefit; default to bypass compression for sub-10ms SLO routes
notes_for_reviewers: Look specifically at 'label_alias' and canonicalization approach. We prefer stable, idempotent transforms to avoid downstream re-ingestion. Verify DLQ schema contains tenant_id, request_id, schema_version, and first_seen timestamp.
